who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent, lane proofs-1113
where: the daemon's start on a home that holds state (blaze serve; the store's buffer pool), blaze-vm
what: `blaze prove -p blaze-core --json` with a release build of 7c585447d4 on a home another build of this lane had written 20 minutes before (BLAZE_HOME=/root/wt/proofs-1113/home: journal 2.4 MB, a daemon image, a store; written by a debug build of the tree before its merge with main 9c1311df11) started a daemon that never listened. The client gave up after 60 s: `the daemon (blaze serve, pid 3400734) was started and did not listen at .../v2.sock: it was reading its state (the VFS journal, the daemon image and the store) for 60s, inside wait (function=signal store.pool.unpinned, awaits=signal store.pool.unpinned, 0.0s open)`. The daemon stayed: 6 min 26 s after its start it had used 5 s of CPU and none in a 3 s sample, 156 threads asleep (two named `store pool load pool`), nothing of its own in serve.log, nothing in the home's `stalls/`. It held serve.lock, so the next command's daemon waited 300 s and ended (`still holds .../serve.lock after 300s`), and `blaze stop` could not reach it (`nothing listens at ...v2.sock`). SIGTERM did not end it within a second; `kill -9` did. Reproduced the same day without `blaze prove` and without this branch: main's installed build on the VM (/root/inst/main, built 05:23 UTC), a fresh home of its own, in a checkout of blaze: `blaze check -p blaze-rng` (17 s, ok), `blaze stop` (ok, `wrote the daemon image ... 5.9 MiB`), `blaze check -p blaze-rng` again: `the daemon (blaze serve, pid 3560448) was started and did not listen ... for 60s, inside wait (function=signal store.pool.unpinned ...)`; a minute in, that daemon had used no CPU, 157 threads asleep, two named `store pool load pool`. This branch's build at 7c585447d4 did the same on three homes. The recipe is /Volumes/Projects/blaze-proofs-1113-notes/restartvm.sh.
cost: one 25-minute VM cycle of the dogfood run; the same command on a fresh home is the rerun
cause: not known. A lead from reading the code, not measured: the wait is `Shared::pin_room_within` (crates/blaze-cas/src/read.rs), a read waiting at the pinned bound for the store's `tidy` to let pins go, 100 ticks of 50 ms and then the read fails; if nothing lets pins go while the daemon reads its state, each read there waits its whole five seconds. Not checked: whether main at 4d4837eec6 still does it, whether a small project does (the smoke's hello-world never restarts on its home), what the bound and the pins were.
whys: a daemon that cannot finish reading its state waits on a signal with no bound a watchdog sees: the stall report and the typed failure both live in the serving loop, which had not started; the client knows only that nothing listened; the daemon's own deadline for its start is not there, so the lock outlives the failure
class: a wait before the daemon serves (reading the journal, the image, the store) has no deadline and no watchdog, so a start that cannot finish is a silent process holding the state's lock
prevention: the start is one bounded step: the daemon gives itself the deadline the client already has (60 s), and at it writes what it was waiting on to serve.log, lets go of serve.lock and exits with a typed code; the watchdog thread starts before the state is read. Not built. And the smoke restarts: after `stop`, one more `blaze run` on the same home, so a daemon that cannot start on its own state fails the quote a merge carries. Not built.
workaround: kill the pid the client's error names; a fresh BLAZE_HOME for every run that follows a `blaze stop`
